ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an ideal operational amplifier proportional amplification circuit. The input voltage ui is connected from the lower left through resistor R2 to the non-inverting input terminal “+” of the op-amp. The output terminal is on the right side, labeled uo. The inverting input terminal “-” is connected to a voltage-dividing feedback network: the upper side is connected to the output terminal through feedback resistor Rf, and the left side is grounded through resistor R1. Reasoning: The problem requires short-circuiting the feedback resistor Rf and opening the grounded resistor R1. After Rf is short-circuited, the output terminal is directly connected to the inverting input terminal; after R1 is opened, the inverting terminal is no longer grounded through the resistor, and the original feedback voltage-dividing network disappears. The input current of an ideal op-amp is 0, so there is no voltage drop across R2, and the voltage at the non-inverting input terminal v+ = ui. Under the action of negative feedback, the ideal op-amp satisfies v- = v+. Also because v- and the output terminal are directly connected by a short-circuit line, uo = v- = v+ = ui. Therefore the voltage amplification factor Au = uo/ui = 1.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the op-amp has ui entering the + input through R2, uo taken at the output, and the - input connected to a feedback branch Rf and a grounding branch R1. Then apply the textual changes: replace Rf by a wire and open-circuit the grounding resistor. With Rf shorted, the output is directly tied to the - input; with the ground branch disconnected, no feedback divider remains. Since the ideal op-amp input draws no current, there is no voltage drop across R2, so v+ = ui. Negative feedback forces v- = v+, and because v- is the same node as the output, uo = ui. Therefore the voltage amplification factor is 1.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Direct circuit-topology reduction: identify the modified op-amp as a unity-gain voltage follower rather than using the original non-inverting gain formula.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the diagram as an ideal op-amp with the input signal ui applied through R2 to the non-inverting (+) input, the output uo on the right, and a feedback path Rf from output to the inverting (-) input; also note the inverting input has a resistor R1 to ground in the original drawing.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question statement to know the modifications to impose: Rf is shorted and the grounding resistor R/R1 is disconnected, and the requested quantity is the voltage amplification factor.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: For an ideal op-amp with negative feedback, v- = v+ and input currents are zero. A shorted feedback resistor makes the output node directly connected to the inverting input. Disconnecting the grounding resistor removes the divider to ground. Thus the circuit becomes a voltage follower, so uo = ui and the voltage gain is 1.
